prerequisites: Familiarity with common user-level computer programs

learning_outcomes.text: Calculate the maximum resistance of machine elements in static and dynamic stress states.
Design and calculate shafts and power shafts.
Select the most appropriate joining and support elements for shafts and axles.
Perform the calculation and design of power transmissions using flexible elements.
Perform the design and verification of gearwheels for a power transmission using gears.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to design. Safety in design.
Practical calculation of resistance. Static Resistance
Rigid transmissions. Gears. Design, calculation and verification
Simplified calculation method of Henriot cylindrical gears
Simplified calculation method for conical gears
Calculation of shafts under bending, torsion, and combined bending and torsion
assessment_rules: To pass the subject, a total grade equal to or greater than 5 out of 10 must be obtained from the sum of the three assessment items. It is a requirement to obtain a minimum score of 4 points out of 10 in the final theoretical-practical exam. Otherwise, the grade for the call will be the minimum between the score obtained with the previous formula and 4.0. For extraordinary calls, the same evaluation criteria apply, maintaining the scores obtained in laboratory and classroom practices, and a new exam with a minimum score of 4 out of 10 is taken. For differentiated evaluation, a single exam covers expositive classes and classroom practices (90%) and laboratory practices (10%).
